Hello! I'm so glad you're here. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a truly overwhelming and life-changing experience. It's completely normal to have a mix of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of support that might be helpful to you. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can give us valuable insights into your emotional well-being during the postpartum period.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and is a safe space for you to express yourself freely. I'm here to listen and support you without judgment, and I want to assure you that my goal is to provide you with the best possible care and resources to help you navigate this new chapter in your life.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your feelings and emotions over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Don't worry; there are no right or wrong answers. This is simply a conversation to help us understand your postpartum experience better.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling a bit down or overwhelmed?

(sighing) Honestly, I've been feeling really tired and overwhelmed most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard to enjoy things like I used to. Even simple things like taking a shower or eating a meal feel like chores now. I've been having trouble sleeping, and when I do, I wake up with these anxious thoughts about my baby's safety. It's like, what if something happens to her while I'm sleeping? What if I'm not doing enough for her? (pausing, looking down) It's hard to explain, but I just feel really sad and discouraged a lot of the time. Like, I'll be playing with my baby, and she'll be smiling at me, and I'll start crying because I just feel so guilty for not being happier. I feel like I should be enjoying every moment of this, but it's just not feeling that way right now. (looking up, tears in my eyes) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head) Not as much as I used to, unfortunately. I mean, I still find some things funny, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit. Even when my husband tries to make me laugh, it's just not the same. I'll smile or chuckle, but it's not a deep, belly laugh like I used to have. And sometimes, I'll be looking at my baby, and she'll be doing something adorable, but instead of laughing, I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm happy to see her happy, but I'm also just so overwhelmed and sad. (sighing) I miss feeling carefree and being able to laugh easily. It's like, that part of me is just gone right now. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head slightly) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like another thing to worry about. Like, my husband will suggest we go for a walk or something, and I'll think, "Okay, that sounds nice," but then I'll start worrying about the baby's schedule and whether she'll be hungry or tired, and it just feels like too much. (pausing) I don't really feel like I'm looking forward to things like I used to. Even things that I used to enjoy, like reading or watching a movie, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. (sighing) It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really enjoying anything. (looking up, with a hint of sadness) It's hard to explain, but it's just like the joy is missing from things that used to bring me happiness.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah. That's been happening a lot lately. I feel like I'm always wondering if I'm doing something wrong, or if I'm not doing enough for the baby. Like, if she's crying, I'll think, "What did I do wrong? Is she hungry? Is she tired? Is she uncomfortable?" And even if my husband or someone else tries to reassure me that I'm doing a good job, I'll still feel like it's my fault somehow. (sighing) It's like, I'm always second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm good enough as a mom. And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I'll think, "I'm a terrible mom and a terrible wife because I'm not keeping the house clean enough." (shaking my head) It's just this constant feeling of guilt and self-doubt, like I'm not measuring up somehow. (looking up, with tears in my eyes) It's really hard to shake off that feeling, you know?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's been happening a lot. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if the baby gets sick? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if something happens to my husband and I'm left to take care of the baby on my own? (taking a deep breath) It's just this constant stream of worried thoughts that I don't know how to turn off. And it's not just during the day, it's at night too. I'll be lying in bed, trying to sleep, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. (shaking my head) It's exhausting, you know? I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is just wired to worry now. Even when everything is fine, I'll still find something to worry about. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop or something. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I feel like I'm going crazy, to be honest.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes, that's happened to me too. I'll be doing something normal, like taking care of the baby or making dinner, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of panic. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (placing my hand on my chest) It's like, my body just takes over, and I feel like I'm losing control. And it's not just when I'm alone, it's happened when I'm with my husband or other people too. (looking down, embarrassed) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of fear wash over me, like something terrible is going to happen to her. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my own safety, or my husband's safety, or just the general safety of the world, I guess. (shaking my head) It's just this constant feeling of being on edge, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. (taking a deep breath) And it's hard to explain, but it's like my mind is just racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I don't know how to calm it down. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's really frightening, to be honest.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yes. That's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, keeping the house clean, cooking meals, being a good wife... it's just all so overwhelming. (sighing) And it's not just the practical things, it's the emotional stuff too. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not living up to it. I'm tired all the time, I'm anxious, I'm worried... I just feel like I'm failing at everything. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And it's hard to ask for help, because I feel like I should be able to do it all on my own. But the truth is, I'm just not coping. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart. (taking a deep breath) It's a really scary feeling, like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop or something. (shaking my head) I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? Like, I wish I could feel confident and capable, instead of just feeling like I'm drowning all the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything that's worrying me. (sighing) And it's not just worries about the baby, it's worries about everything. I'll think about my relationships, my health, my future... just everything. (shaking my head) My mind just won't shut off, and it's hard to relax. (pausing, looking down) And even when I do fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so disturbing. I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge, and it's hard to shake that feeling off. (looking up) It's like, I'm just not getting any rest, even when I am sleeping. And it's affecting everything, you know? I'm tired all the time, I'm irritable, I'm just not myself. (tearfully) I just wish I could sleep like a normal person again, you know? I wish I could just lie down and rest without all these thoughts racing through my head. (wiping away a tear) Sorry, it's just... it's just really hard right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so sad and miserable, and I don't know how to shake it off. (pausing, looking down) It's like, I'll be doing something with the baby, and she'll be smiling at me, and I'll just start crying. (shaking my head) It's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be with my husband, or with friends, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just carrying this weight around with me all the time, and I don't know how to put it down. (looking up, tears in my eyes) Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel so grateful to have her, but at the same time, I'll feel so sad and overwhelmed. It's like, I'm happy and sad at the same time, and it's just really confusing. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've had thoughts, too... thoughts about not being a good enough mom, or not being able to take care of the baby. (looking down, feeling ashamed) Sometimes I'll think about just... escaping, or something. Not that I would ever do anything to hurt myself, but just... (trailing off, feeling tears fall) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about this stuff. (sniffling)
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling tears well up in my eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be doing something, and suddenly I'll just start crying. (pausing, looking down) It's not just when I'm sad, either. I'll be happy, or I'll be watching a movie, or I'll be talking to someone, and I'll just start crying. (shaking my head) It's like, my emotions are just really close to the surface right now, and it doesn't take much to set me off. (sighing) I've been crying in front of my husband, in front of my friends... even in front of the baby. (feeling a pang of guilt) I just feel so bad about it, because I don't want the baby to see me like this. I want to be strong for her, but it's just hard right now. (looking up, tears streaming down my face) Sometimes I'll be crying, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just stop crying?" (sobbing) But it's just... it's like my body is just releasing all this tension and stress, and I don't know how to make it stop. (covering my face with my hands) I'm just so tired of crying all the time. I'm tired of feeling sad and overwhelmed. I just want to feel like myself again. (sobbing uncontrollably)
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, feeling a mix of emotions) Yes... I have had those thoughts. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've ever thought about before. But lately, when things have been feeling really overwhelming, I've had these... these fleeting thoughts of just wanting to escape, or wanting to make the pain stop. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's not that I want to hurt myself, it's just that I feel so trapped and so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. (shaking my head) I know it's not rational, and I know it's not something I would ever act on. But the thoughts are there, and they're scary. (pausing, feeling a sense of shame) I'm scared to admit it, because I don't want people to think I'm crazy, or that I'm not a good mom. But at the same time, I feel like I need to be honest about how I'm feeling, because maybe that's the only way I can get help. (looking down, feeling tears fall) I just feel so lost and so alone, and I don't know how to make it better. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But I do know that I don't want to hurt myself, and I don't want to do anything that would harm my baby or my family. I just want to feel better, and I want to be able to be the mom and the person I'm supposed to be. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) Can you help me? Can you help me make these thoughts go away, and help me feel like myself again?
